title: Study on the use of colchicine to reduce inflammation after deep vein thrombosis
official: Colchicine to Quench the Inflammatory Response after Deep Vein Thrombosis: The CONQUER-DVT Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of low-dose colchicine 0.5 mg versus placebo once daily in reducing the risk of Post-thrombotic syndrome (PTS) in patients with proximal lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT).
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 18 years of age or older
2. First, acute, symptomatic proximal (popliteal or more proximal vein) objectively-confirmed DVT of the lower extremity
3. Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Any contraindication to colchicine as per summary of product characteristics (SmPC)
2. Known active cancer
3. Any of the following as measured within the past 1-3 months or at screening: alanine or aspartate aminotransferase >3x upper limit of normal (ULN); total bilirubin >2x ULN; creatinine clearance, calculated using Cockcroft-Gault formula, <30 mL/min
4. Presence of HIV infection
5. Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients
6. Participation in another interventional trial within the past 30 days or 5  half-lives of the study drug, whichever is longer
7. Unwilling to provide consent
8. Pregnancy, breastfeeding or may be considering pregnancy during the study period or women of childbearing potential unwilling to use appropriate contraception during sex
9. Use of medications with known significant drug-to-drug interactions with colchicine including but not limited to erythromycin or clarithromycin
10. History of an allergic reaction or significant sensitivity to colchicine
11. Requirement of colchicine for other indications
12. Active or chronic diarrhoea, or documented inflammatory bowel disease (i.e., Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis), collagenous colitis/irritable bowel syndrome, or existing blood dyscrasias
13. Known or suspected, recent (<30 days) or active infections (acute or chronic)
14. History of cirrhosis, chronic active hepatitis, or severe liver disease
15. Recent (<30 days) or chronic use of systemic (oral, intravenous) immunosuppressive drugs (including but not limited to steroids, tumor necrosis factor-alpha blockers, cyclosporine)
